MAJAZ:v1p14/r14.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r14.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r14.claim: Here ما functions like a noun; the sense is إن صنيعهم كيد ساحر (‘their craft is a sorcerer’s trick’).
MAJAZ:v1p14/r14.anchor: قال: «إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر» (20/ 69) . فمعنى «ما» معنى الاسم، مجازه إن صنيعهم كيد ساحر.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r6.claim: God directs Moses to place his staff down; it swallows the magicians' trick, expressing the principle that magic cannot overcome truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r6.anchor: magic can never combat the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r7.claim: The author states the broader rule that a magician never succeeds, since magic deceives the eye and imagination.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r7.anchor: a magician never succeeds because this is a fact

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r8.claim: Magicians may fool crowds briefly but, unlike prophets, do not contribute to society; prophetic miracles and character carry grandeur.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r8.anchor: they can fool the masses for a few days with their tricks

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r1.claim: Prophets stand at humanity's pinnacle; even enemies attest to their character, and their preaching opens a new historical era.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r1.anchor: even their enemies vouch for their high character

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r2.claim: The author contrasts prophets with magicians, asking whether any magician has contributed to any sphere of life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r2.anchor: Has there ever been a magician who has even contributed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r3.claim: The logical distinction between magic and miracle made by theologians is a useless exercise; the decisive factor is what people with sight perceive.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r3.anchor: difference between magic and miracle as explained by our theologians is a useless exercise

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r6.claim: The wording ‘what is in your right hand’ rather than ‘your staff’ invokes the auspicious and blessed sense of the right hand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r6.anchor: وألق ما في يمينك لم يأت التركيب وألق عصاك لما في لفظ اليمين من معنى اليمن والبركة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ما في يمينك may belittle the single small staff against many ropes, yet God’s power lets it swallow them all.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r7.anchor: جائز أن يكون تصغيرا لها أي لا تبال بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم، وألق العويد الفرد الصغير الجرم الذي في يمينك فإنه بقدرة الله يتلقفها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r8.claim: Alternatively, the wording magnifies the object in Moses’ hand as more powerful than all their large, numerous objects; the author calls this elaboration unhelpful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r8.anchor: وجائز أن يكون تعظيما لها أي لا تحتفل بهذه الأجرام الكبيرة الكثيرة فإن في يمينك شيئا أعظم منها كلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r9.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhshari’s detailed alternative over-elaborate and without useful force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r9.anchor: وهو تكثير وخطابه لا طائل في ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r10.claim: The agreement in تلقف follows the meaning of ما, namely the feminine العصا; agreement with its form would instead use yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r10.anchor: وفي قوله تلقف جمل على معنى ما لا على لفظها إذ أطلقت ما على العصا والعصا مؤنثة، ولو حمل على اللفظ لكان بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r11.claim: The majority read تلقف with open lām, doubled qāf, and jussive fāʾ as the response to the command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تلقف بفتح اللام وتشديد القاف مجزوما على جواب الأمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r12.speaker: ابن عامر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r12.claim: Ibn Amir has the same form but raises the fāʾ, either as a new clause or a circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر كذلك وبرفع الفاء على الاستئناف أو على الحال من الملقى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر، وحفص، وعصمة عن عاصم، وقنبل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r13.claim: Abu Jafar, Hafs, and Isma read with still lām and fāʾ and light qāf; Qunbul is also reported to double qāf, intending يتلقف.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وحفص وعصمة عن عاصم تلقف بإسكان اللام والفاء وتخفيف القاف وعن قنبل أنه كان يشدد من تلقف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r1.claim: The majority read كيد in the nominative as a relative pronoun with an omitted antecedent, or as a verbal noun meaning ‘their making was sorcery.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور كيد بالرفع على أن ما موصولة بمعنى الذي والعائد محذوف، ويحتمل أن تكون ما مصدرية أي إن صنعتم كيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد، وحميد، وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r2.claim: They read كيد سحر in the accusative, making it the object of صنعوا and treating ما as a particle that prepares the construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وزيد بن علي كيد سحر بالنصب مفعولا لصنعوا وما مهيئة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r3.speaker: أبو بحرية، والأعمش، وطلحة، وابن أبي ليلى، وخلف في اختياره، وابن عيسى الأصبهاني، وابن جبير الأنطاكي، وابن جرير، وحمزة، والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r3.claim: They read سِحر with kasra and still ḥāʾ: it can mean ‘possessor of magic,’ describe people so steeped in it they are magic itself, or specify that the plot is sorcery rather than another kind of trick.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو بحرية والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وخلف في اختياره وابن عيسى الأصبهاني وابن جبير الأنطاكي وابن جرير وحمزة والكسائي سحر بكسر السين وإسكان الحاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r4.claim: The majority use the active participle ساحر in the singular because the group performed one kind of magic, namely the ropes and staffs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ساحر اسم فاعل من سحر، وأفرد ساحر من حيث أن فعل الجميع نوع واحد من السحر، وذلك الحبال والعصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the singular carries a generic meaning, not a count; pluralizing would suggest that number is the point, as in ولا يفلح الساحر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r5.anchor: لأن القصد في هذا الكلام إلى معنى الجنسية لا إلى معنى العدد، فلو جمع لخيل أن المقصود هو العدد ألا ترى أن قوله ولا يفلح الساحر أي هذا الجنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r6.claim: The definite article in الساحر resumes the earlier indefinite ساحر, as in the cited example of a messenger sent to Pharaoh and Pharaoh disobeying the messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r6.anchor: وعرف في قوله ولا يفلح الساحر لأنه عاد على ساحر النكرة قبله كقوله كما أرسلنا إلى فرعون رسولا فعصى فرعون الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the indefinite modifier in سعي دنيا and أمر دنيا/آخرة as indefiniteness of the annexed noun, comparing a saying from Umar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r7.anchor: إنما نكر يعني أولا من أجل تنكير المضاف لا من أجل تنكيره في نفسه كقول العجاج: في سعي دنيا طال ما قد مدت وفي حديث عمر رضي الله عنه: لا في أمر دنيا ولا في أمر آخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r8.claim: The author says al-ʿAjjaj’s phrase is poetic necessity because دنيا is the feminine of أدنى, and the Umar report may reflect a narrator’s corruption.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r8.anchor: وقول العجاج: في سعي دنيا، محمول على الضرورة إذ دنيا تأنيث الأدنى، ولا يستعمل تأنيثه إلا بالألف واللام أو بالإضافة وأما قول عمر فيحتمل أن يكون من تحريف الرواة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r9.claim: لا يفلح means a sorcerer never reaches his goal wherever he turns; another group says it means he is killed wherever found, which is the outcome of failure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r9.anchor: ومعنى ولا يفلح لا يظفر ببغيته حيث أتى أي حيث توجه وسلك. وقالت فرقة معناه أن الساحر بقتل حيث تقف وهذا جزاء من عدم الفلاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r10.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r10.claim: Another reading has أين أتى in place of حيث أتى.

AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud's reading has أين أتى instead of حيث أتى; Arabic also uses جئتك من أين لا تعلم and من حيث لا تعلم.
AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r5.anchor: وقال {الساحر حيث أتى} وفي حرف ابن مسعود {أين أتى} وتقول العرب: "جئتك من أين لا تعلم" و"من حيث لا تعلم".

TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r4.claim: Calling the staff what is in Moses' right hand points to the lack of intrinsic reality in things: by God's will it can be a staff or a living serpent.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r4.anchor: فإن فيه إشارة إلى أن ليس للشيء من الحقيقة إلا ما أراد الله فإن أراد لما في اليمين أن يكون عصا

TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r5.claim: Calling the magicians' serpents what they made frames the contest as God's unrestricted power against human fabrication, which is false and vanishing before God's word.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r5.anchor: يشير إلى أن المغالبة واقعة بين تلك القدرة المطلقة التي تتبعها الأشياء في أساميها وحقائقها وبين هذا الصنع البشري

TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r6.claim: The staff's swallowing displays Moses' superiority to the senses, while the verse's conclusion displays his superiority in reality because falsehood has no reality and truth need not fear it.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r6.anchor: بيان لكونه عليه السلام أعلى بحسب ظاهر الحس كما أن في ذيله بيانا لكونه أعلى بحسب الحقيقة إذ لا حقيقة للباطل

TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r7.claim: The description of their work as a sorcerer's trick explains its being swallowed and shows why Moses' miracle prevails: their magic lacks reality while his sign has it.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r7.anchor: لأن ما معهم كيد ساحر لا حقيقة له وما معه آية معجزة ذات حقيقة والحق يعلو ولا يعلى عليه

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r1.claim: A sorcerer gains only an illusion for observers, so an unreal undertaking cannot yield genuine success or happiness; this is the major premise behind the claim that sorcerers do not prosper.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r1.anchor: فإن الذي يناله الساحر بسحره خيال من الناظرين باطل لا حقيقة له ولا فلاح ولا سعادة حقيقية

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r2.claim: The claim that sorcerers do not prosper resembles statements that God does not guide wrongdoers and derives from the principle that falsehood vanishes and God effaces it while establishing truth.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r2.anchor: والجميع من فروع إن الباطل كان زهوقا الإسراء 81، ويمح الله الباطل

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r3.claim: Falsehood keeps embellishing itself as truth, but truth eventually erases it; Moses' staff swallowing the magic illustrates a pattern applying to every falsehood and the truth that destroys it.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r3.anchor: فلا يزال الباطل يزين أمورا ويشبهها بالحق ولا يزال الحق يمحوه ويلقف ما أظهره لوهم الناظرين

RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r1.claim: Rāzī explains the singular “magician” generically: the wording concerns the class, not a number of individual magicians.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r1.anchor: لأن القصد في هذا الكلام إلى معنى الجنسية لا إلى معنى العدد

RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r2.claim: The indefinite first mention makes the magicians' work one kind of magic; the definite second mention generalizes the futility to every kind, which is more emphatic.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r2.anchor: هذا الذي أتوا به قسم واحد من أقسام السحر وجميع أقسام السحر لا فائدة فيه

RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74/r3.claim: Rāzī raises the inference that magic cannot attain any aim, good or evil, so the verse seems to deny magic altogether; he refers readers to his earlier discussion of magic in al-Baqara.

STUDYQURAN:20:69/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r1.claim: Moses’ staff devoured the sorcerers’ deceptions, exposing their work as false.
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r1.anchor: When Moses cast his staff, it devoured all their deceptions (7:117) and whatsoever they did was shown to be false (7:118)

STUDYQURAN:20:69/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r2.claim: Moses’ statement parallels his declaration in 10:77 about the ultimate futility of sorcery.
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r2.anchor: See also 10:77, where Moses makes a similar statement about the ultimate futility of the work of sorcerers

STUDYQURAN:20:69/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r3.claim: After their defeat the sorcerers turned back humbled; the commentary also points to 20:89.
STUDYQURAN:20:69/r3.anchor: After the sorcerers were defeated, they turned back, humbled (7:119). See also 20:89c

TAB-FULL:v16p111/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p111/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p111/r1.claim: Most Medinan and Basran readers and some Kufans read ساحر with alif, while most Kufans read سحر without it. Al-Tabari accepts both as close in meaning: the sorcerer plots through illusion and sorcery deceives by illusion.
TAB-FULL:v16p111/r1.anchor: والقول في ذلك عندي أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان متقاربتا المعنى، وذلك أن الكيد هو المكر والخدعة

TAB-FULL:v16p111/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p111/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p111/r2.claim: A reading with accusative كيد and uninflected سحر is attributed to some, but al-Tabari rejects it because the authoritative readers agree against it.
TAB-FULL:v16p111/r2.anchor: وقد ذكر عن بعضهم أنه قرأ: «كيد سحر» بنصب كيد

TAB-FULL:v16p112/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p112/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p112/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says no sorcerer succeeds anywhere; some interpret this as killing the sorcerer wherever found. A Basran grammarian reports Ibn Masud’s أين أتى reading, while another grammarian treats examples like من حيث لا تعلم as queries asking where water and pasture are.
TAB-FULL:v16p112/r1.anchor: وقال غيره من أهل العربية الأول: جزاء يقتل الساحر حيث أتى وأين أتى

TAB-FULL:v16p113/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r1.claim: The narrative omits an understood clause: Moses threw his staff, which swallowed what the magicians had made.
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r1.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام متروك قد استغني بدلالة ما ترك عليه وهو: فألقى موسى عصاه، فتلقفت ما صنعوا

TAB-FULL:v16p113/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r2.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r2.claim: Saʿid reports that Moses’ staff became a huge serpent, swallowed all the magicians’ ropes and staffs, then returned to a staff; the magicians prostrated, while Pharaoh claimed Moses taught them and threatened crosswise amputation and crucifixion.
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r2.anchor: عن سعيد، قال: لما اجتمعوا وألقوا ما في أيديهم من السحر خيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

TAB-FULL:v16p113/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the staff ate every snake the magicians made, after which they prostrated and professed faith in the Lord of the worlds.
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r4.anchor: عن السدي، {فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى}

TAB-FULL:v16p113/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r5.claim: Wahb reports that Moses feared the apparent moving serpents, but God reassured him; his staff swallowed every rope and staff before becoming a staff again, and the magicians believed it could not be sorcery since it defeated them.
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r5.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، {فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى}

TABRISI:20:71/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r1.speaker: ابن ذكوان
TABRISI:20:71/r1.claim: Ibn Dhakwan reads تلقف with رفع; others use جزم, with Hafs reading it lightly and the rest doubling the قاف, while al-Bazzi's and Ibn Fulayh's transmissions from Ibn Kathir also double the initial تاء.
TABRISI:20:71/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن ذكوان تلقف بالرفع والباقون بالجزم إلا أن حفصا يقرؤها خفيفة

TABRISI:20:71/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r2.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
TABRISI:20:71/r2.claim: The Kufans except Asim read كيد سحر without an alif; the others read ساحر with an alif.
TABRISI:20:71/r2.anchor: وقرأ كيد سحر بغير ألف أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون ساحر بالألف

TABRISI:20:71/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r3.claim: The رفع reading treats the verb as a circumstantial clause, attributable either to the thrower or to the thrown object, the staff, feminine by sense; 99:4 offers a similar shift between human addressee and Earth as speaker.
TABRISI:20:71/r3.anchor: بالرفع فإنه يرتفع لأنه في موضع الحال

TABRISI:20:71/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r4.claim: The جزم reading is a conditional answer: if you throw it, it will swallow them.
TABRISI:20:71/r4.anchor: فعلى أن يكون جوابا كأنه قال أن تلقه تلقف

TABRISI:20:71/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r5.claim: Doubling the تاء represents تتلقف and can be understood with either the human addressee or the feminine staff; Tabrisi notes that assimilation seems formally problematic because a sukun would call for a hamzat al-wasl unavailable in the present tense, and reports Ahmad ibn Musa's explanation that the reader begins as in the unassimilated form.
TABRISI:20:71/r5.anchor: ومن شدد التاء فإنما أراد تتلقف

TABRISI:20:71/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r6.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:20:71/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i says لقفت الشيء and its forms mean to take something quickly.
TABRISI:20:71/r6.anchor: يقال لقفت الشيء وتلقفته والتقفته إذا أخذته بسرعة

TABRISI:20:71/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r9.claim: إن is separated from ما because ما is relative and صنعوا its clause, with a deleted resumptive; alternatively ما is a particle and the phrase means إن صنعهم.
TABRISI:20:71/r9.anchor: إن مفصول من ما صنعوا لأن ما ههنا موصولة

TABRISI:20:71-72/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r16.claim: What Moses holds in his right hand is his staff.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r16.anchor: يعني العصا { تلقف ما صنعوا } أي تبتلع ما صنعوا فيه

TABRISI:20:71-72/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r17.claim: The staff swallows the ropes and staffs used in their magic; those physical objects themselves were not made by the magicians.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r17.anchor: تبتلع ما صنعوا فيه من الحبال والعصي لأن الحبال والعصي أجسام ليست من صنعهم

TABRISI:20:71-72/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r18.claim: The staff became a serpent, circled the ranks so everyone saw it, swallowed all the ropes and staffs, then Moses took it and it returned to its former shape.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r18.anchor: ولما ألقى عصاه صارت حية وطافت حول الصفوف حتى رآها الناس كلهم

TABRISI:20:71-72/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r19.claim: Their production was a magician’s trick, device, or stratagem.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r19.anchor: أي أن الذي صنعوه أو أن صنيعهم كيد ساحر أي مكره وحيلته

TABRISI:20:71-72/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r20.claim: The magician cannot attain his aim because magic has no reality; alternatively, he cannot succeed with magic wherever he goes.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r20.anchor: وقيل: لا يفوز الساحر حيث أتى بسحره لأن الحق يبطله

THALABI:v6p253/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r4.speaker: القاسم بن أبي برزة
THALABI:v6p253/r4.claim: Qasim reports that Pharaoh assembled seventy thousand magicians, whose ropes and staffs seemed to move; Moses' staff swallowed them, and the magicians prostrated after seeing Paradise, Hell, and their rewards. The same report recounts Pharaoh's wife persisting in faith after being shown her home in Paradise, whereupon her soul was taken and a stone cast on her lifeless body.
THALABI:v6p253/r4.anchor: عن القاسم بن أبي برزة قال: جمع فرعون سبعين ألف ساحر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the jussive reading answers the command; the indicative is also possible as a circumstantial clause meaning the staff will swallow it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: (القراءة بالجزم (¬5)، جواب الأمر، ويجوز الرفع على معنى الحال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains Ibn ʿĀmir’s indicative as a circumstantial clause of either the agent Moses or the object, the staff; the action may be attributed to its cause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r2.anchor: وشرحه أبو علي فقال: (وجه قراءة من قرأ: {تلقف} بالرفع، وهي قراءة ابن عامر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r3.claim: For the object analysis, Abū ʿAlī allows a future action in a circumstantial clause and cites the sacrificial animal reaching the Kaʿba in 5:95.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r3.anchor: كما جاء في التنزيل: {هديا بالغ الكعبة} [المائدة: 95]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r4.claim: The feminine talqafu follows the meaning of what is in Moses’s hand, namely the staff; the jussive can be command-response or an address to Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459#2/r4.anchor: وقال: ({تلقف} على التأنيث، حملا للكلام على المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r1.claim: The magicians’ work was a magician’s trick, an illusion with no real substance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر} أي: الذي صنعوه كيد ساحر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r2.claim: A variant reads kaydu siḥr; sahir is stronger because the plot belongs to a magician, while siḥr attributes it by extension to magic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r2.anchor: وقرئ: كيد سحر (¬4). وساحر أقوى؛ لأن الكيد للساحر في الحقيقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains kaydu siḥr as the plot of one who practices magic, like a silk shirt or brocade robe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ: كيد سحر، أضاف الكيد إلى السحر على التوسع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the verse as saying that a magician does not prosper wherever he may be.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (ولا يسعد الساحر حيث ما كان)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r5.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r5.claim: Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Bajalī reports that the Prophet said to kill a magician if caught, then recited this verse and said he is not safe wherever found; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r5.anchor: وروى جندب بن عبد الله البجلي (¬3): أن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "إذا أخذتم الساحر فاقتلوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq says a magician should be killed wherever found and reports that this is also the jurists’ position; al-Farrāʾ gives a similar interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p460/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (معناه حيث كان الساحر يجب أن يقتل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r10.claim: What the magicians made was a magician's scheme; a magician does not succeed wherever he goes.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r10.anchor: ولا يسعد الساحر حيث ما كان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r11.claim: Moses cast his staff, which swallowed everything they made; the sorcerers then fell into prostration.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r11.anchor: فألقى موسى عصاه فتلقفت كل الذي صنعوه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r8.claim: What Moses held in his right hand was the staff.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r9.claim: The staff swallowed the ropes and staffs the magicians made.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r9.anchor: تلقف ما صنعوا} [طه: 69] يعني العصا. وقوله: تلقف، تأكل حبالهم وعصيهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r10.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says the staff swallowed them with its mouth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r10.anchor: فيما حدثني قرة بن خالد عن الحسن، تلقفه بفيها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r11.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r11.claim: Al-Hasan explains the sorcerer as failing wherever he may be.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r12.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r12.claim: Another gloss is wherever the sorcerer comes.

QASHANI:20:64-70/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r6.claim: The staff in the right hand signifies the intellect under control, joined to the light of holiness and illuminated by truth; it swallows the sorcerers' ornate false doubts.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r6.anchor: ما في ضبط عقلك من النفس المؤتلفة بشعاع القدس المضيئة بنور الحق

QASHANI:20:64-70/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r7.claim: Sorcery is mere deception and embellishment.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r7.anchor: { إنما صنعوا } وتلقفوا { كيد ساحر } أي: تمويه وتزوير

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.claim: Israelite presence in Egypt and Moses' effort to lead them back to their homeland created political anxiety for Pharaoh's government and a psychological warfare setting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.anchor: İsrâiloğulları’nın Mısır’daki varlığının ve Hz. Mûsâ tarafından eski yurtlarına götürülmeleri için ortaya konan çabanın Firavun yönetimi nezdinde oluşturduğu siyasî kaygılar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.claim: Because magic deeply affected the masses and had a religious dimension in that society, foregrounding it as the contest could help establish Moses' prophethood and leadership.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.anchor: o günün şartları içinde geniş kitleleri derinden etkilemekte olan ve dinî bir hüviyet de taşıyan sihir olgusunu ön plana çıkaran bir mücadele metodu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.claim: Pharaoh and his elite regarded magic as their most effective weapon against monotheism, pressured and rewarded the magicians, and expected an absolute victory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.anchor: sihri tevhid çağrısına karşı kullanabilecekleri en etkili silâh olarak görüyorlar ve sihirbazlara bir taraftan baskı, bir taraftan da teşvik uygulayarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.claim: God equipped Moses with miracles that nullified the magicians' skills, giving Pharaoh and his circle another opportunity to be tested.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.anchor: İlâhî irade böyle bir atmosferde Hz. Mûsâ’yı sihirbazların bütün hünerlerini boşa çıkaracak mûcizelerle donatıp Firavun ve çevresindekilere bir imtihan fırsatı daha vermek şeklinde tecelli etmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.claim: The commentary points readers to compare the Qur'anic account with the Biblical account of the episode.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.anchor: bu olayla ilgili bilgilerin Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’tekilerle karşılaştırılması için bk. A‘râf 7/103-126

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r15.claim: Moses' superiority should not be reduced to winning a magic contest; the magicians' undertaking is explicitly not approved by religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r15.anchor: sihirbazların ortaya koydukları çabanın dinen asla tasvip edilmediğine de dikkat çekilmiştir

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r4.claim: The ropes only appeared to be snakes; Moses' staff swallowed the whole mass of ropes, then became a staff again, proving the magicians false.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r4.anchor: فلما خيلوا للناس بإلقاء الحبال أنها حيات ابتلعت عصا موسى جملة أوقار الحبال ، وصار الثعبان عصا كما كان

ITQAN:v4p436/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p436/r8.speaker: ليث
ITQAN:v4p436/r8.claim: Layth says he heard that passages from 10:81, 7:117–122, and 20:69 cure sorcery when recited over water in a vessel and poured on the bewitched person's head.
ITQAN:v4p436/r8.anchor: عن ليث قال ( بلغني أن هؤلاء الآيات شفاء من السحر يقرأن في إناء فيه ماء

ITQAN:v4p522/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p522/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p522/r1.claim: Jundab ibn ʿAbd Allah reports the Prophet saying to kill a sorcerer if found; the Prophet recited this verse and explained it as meaning the sorcerer does not succeed wherever found.
ITQAN:v4p522/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إذا وجدتم الساحر فاقتلوه ) ثم قرأ

FARRA:v2p186/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p186/r1.speaker: التفسير
FARRA:v2p186/r1.claim: An exegetical report says the sorcerer is to be killed wherever he is found.
FARRA:v2p186/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنه يقتل حيثما وجد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#7/r1.claim: Ḥaythu atā means wherever he is.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#7/r1.anchor: {ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى} أي حيث كان.

NAHHAS:v3p48/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p48/r12.claim: Moses' staff swallowed the ropes and staffs, which together had the load of three hundred camels; they vanished and only God knows where they went.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r12.anchor: وكانت حمل ثلاثمائة بعير ثم عادت عصا لا يعلم أحد أين ذهبت الحبال والعصي

NAHHAS:v3p48/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r14.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p48/r14.claim: Abu Ishaq allows تلقف in the indicative as a prospective circumstantial clause.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r14.anchor: قال ويجوز ( تلقف ما صنعوا ) بالرفع يكون فعلا مستقبلا في موضع الحال المقدرة

NAHHAS:v3p48/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r15.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p48/r15.claim: Abu Ishaq allows opening the hamza in أن ما صنعوا, understood causally as because what they made is a magician's trick.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r15.anchor: ويجوز أن ما صنعوا بفتح الهمزة أي لأن ما ( كيد ساحر ) بالرفع

NAHHAS:v3p48/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p48/r16.claim: In كيد ساحر, كيد may be the predicate of إن with ما meaning الذي, or ما may be an extra particle that blocks إن from governing.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r16.anchor: بالرفع على خبر إن و ما بمعنى الذي والنصب على أن تكون ما كافة

NAHHAS:v3p48/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r17.speaker: الكوفيون إلا عاصما
NAHHAS:v3p48/r17.claim: The Kufans except Asim read كيد سحر, construing it as an annexation of kind to genus, like ثوب خز.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r17.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون إلا عاصما ( كيد سحر ) على إضافة النوع والجنس كما تقول ثوب خز

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r1.claim: The common reading has open lām, doubled qāf, and jazm on fāʾ as the answer to the command.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بفتح اللام وتشديد القاف وجزم الفاء على جواب الأمر

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r2.speaker: حفص
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r2.claim: Hafs reads with a quiescent lām and a light qāf.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم أن حفصا يقرأ " تلقف " بسكون اللام وتخفيف القاف.

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r3.speaker: ابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r3.claim: Ibn Dhakwan reads the verb in the indicative, as either a circumstantial clause or a new sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن ذكوان هنا " تلقف " بالرفع: إما على الحال، وإما على الاستئناف.

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r4.claim: The verb is feminine because ما refers in sense to the feminine العصا; masculine agreement with ما's grammatical form would have been possible but is not read.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r4.anchor: وأنث الفعل في " تلقف " حملا على معنى " ما " لأن معناها العصا، ولو ذكر ذهابا إلى لفظها لجاز، ولم يقرأ به.

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows Moses himself as the subject, which would make the indicative reading a circumstantial clause describing Moses.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " يجوز أن يكون فاعل " تلقف " ضمير موسى " فعلى هذا يجوز أن يكون " تلقف " في قراءة الرفع حالا من " موسى ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r6.claim: The author considers Abu al-Baqa's subject analysis far-fetched.

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r7.claim: In the common nominative reading, كيد is the predicate of إن; ما is relative, صنعوا its clause with an omitted resumptive, and the sense is 'what they made is a magician's plot.'
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r7.anchor: قوله: { كيد ساحر } العامة على رفع " كيد " على أنه خبر " إن " و " ما " موصولة

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r8.claim: ما may instead be infinitival, making the sense 'their making is a magician's plot' without an omitted resumptive.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون " ما " مصدرية فلا حاجة إلى العائد، والإعراب بحاله.

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r9.speaker: مجاهد وحميد وزيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r9.claim: Mujahid, Humayd, and Zayd ibn ʿAli read كيد in the accusative as an object and take ما as an extra particle preparing the construction.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r9.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وزيد بن على " كيد " بالنصب على أنه مفعول به، و " ما " مزيدة مهيئة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r10.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r10.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read كيد سحر, which can mean a plot of magic-workers, treat the magic itself as the plot for emphasis, or specify the plot's kind.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r10.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان " كيد سحر " على أن المعنى: كيد ذوي سحر، أو جعلوا نفس السحر مبالغة، أو تبيين للكيد؛

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r11.claim: Abu al-Baqa analyzes كيد ساحر as a verbal noun annexed to its agent and كيد سحر as a genus annexed to its type.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r11.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " كيد ساحر " إضافة المصدر إلى الفاعل و " كيد سحر " إضافة الجنس إلى النوع ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains singular ساحر despite a group as generic wording; the plural would suggest that number itself is intended.
SAMIN-DURR:20:69/r12.anchor: وأفرد/ ساحرا، وإن كان المراد به جماعة. قال الزمخشري: " لأن القصد في هذا الكلام إلى معنى الجنسية، لا إلى معنى العدد،

ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r1.claim: The wording kīdu sāḥir is read; Zajjāj also allows kīdu siḥr, and says the accusative opening annamā is not known to him as a reading here; the kasra reading is stronger in meaning.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r1.anchor: ويقرأ (كيد سحر)، ويجوز إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر

ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r2.claim: On the nominative analysis, mā is the subject of inna and kīdu sāḥir is its predicate: what they made is a magician's plot.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r2.anchor: فأما رفع كيد فعلى معنى أن الذي صنعوه كيد ساحر

ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r3.claim: In the accusative analysis, mā prevents inna from governing, and kīda is the object of ṣanaʿū, as in innamā ḍarabtu Zaydan.

ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r4.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r4.claim: One explanation of ḥaythu atā is wherever the magician may be.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r4.anchor: قالوا معناه حيث كان، وقيل معناه حيث كان الساحر

ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r5.claim: The view that a magician must be killed is also the position of jurists on sorcerers.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367/r5.anchor: وقيل معناه حيث كان الساحر يجب أن يقتل

ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r2.claim: Talaqqaf in the jussive is the reading as an answer to the command; a nominative form is possible as a circumstantial expression but was not read and should not be recited without an established reading.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r2.anchor: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا

ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r1.claim: Razi explains “wherever he may come” to mean that a sorcerer cannot succeed whether pursuing a good or an evil end.
ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r1.anchor: "wherever he may come" - i.e., irrespective of whether he aims at a good or at an evil end (Razi)

ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r2.claim: Asad takes the statement as a categorical condemnation of every practice of magic, regardless of the practitioner's intention.
ASAD-NOTES:20:68#n49/r2.anchor: The above statement implies a categorical condemnation of all endeavours which fall under the heading of "magic"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r1.claim: He says whether إن ما is written joined or separate follows the muṣḥaf, yet observes an apparent rhetorical pattern in the spelling.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r1.anchor: ابتداء يعود الأمر إلى خط المصحف سواء وصل أم فصل لكن المُلاحظ الغريب في هذه الآيات كأنما نحس أن للفصل والوصل غرض بياني

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r3.claim: The joined form fits the magicians' completed act; he gives the joined booty phrase in al-Anfal as a parallel for something already done.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p903/r3.anchor: السحرة صنعوا وانتهى الأمر، وكذلك قوله تعالى

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r1.claim: Ibn Amir alone reads talaqqafu with a raised ending and a doubled qāf, as a present indicative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر وحده: (ما في يمينك تلقف ما) برفع الفاء وتشديد القاف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r2.claim: Hafs from Asim reads the qāf light; the other readers and Abu Bakr from Asim read with a jussive ending.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r2.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم: تلقف خفيفة. وقرأ الباقون وأبو بكر عن عاصم: (تلقف ما) مجزومة الفاء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r3.speaker: النبال عن ابن كثير، والبزي وابن فليح
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r3.claim: Al-Nabbal transmits a light tāʾ from Ibn Kathir, as read to Qunbul; al-Bazzi and Ibn Fuleih transmit doubled tāʾ and qāf.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r3.anchor: وروى النبال عن ابن كثير: ما في يمينك تلقف خفيفة التاء كذلك قرأت على قنبل. وكان [ابن كثير] يشدد التاء [والقاف] في رواية البزي وابن فليح : (ما في يمينك تلقف).

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r4.claim: The raised reading can be a circumstantial clause of the thrower, since Moses’ casting causes the swallowing; Al-Farisi compares this attribution with God’s empowering of the Prophet’s throw.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r4.anchor: فإن جعلته من الفاعل الملقي جعلته المتلقف، وإن كان التلقف في الحقيقة للعصا، ووجه جعل المتلقف للفاعل على أن التلقف بإلقائه كان،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r5.claim: Alternatively, the circumstantial verb can describe the feminine staff, with feminine agreement carried by meaning as in the cited examples.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الحال من المفعول، وقال فيه: (تلقف) على حد قولك: هند تذهب، لأنه حمل الكلام على المعنى،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r6.claim: A circumstantial verb may describe a future event, as in ‘a sacrifice reaching the Kaʿba’ or a man accompanied by a falcon that will hunt tomorrow.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r6.anchor: وجعلت (تلقف) حالا، وإن لم تتلقف بعد، كما جاء في التنزيل: هديا بالغ الكعبة [المائدة/ 95]

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r7.claim: The jussive can be a conditional result, ‘if you cast it, it swallows it’; the form can address the listener or describe the feminine staff.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r7.anchor: وأما (تلقف) فعلى أن يكون جوابا كأنه: إن تلقه تلقف، وكذلك تلقف، ويجوز في (تلقف) وتلقف أن يكون لك أيها المخاطب،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r8.claim: For doubled talaqqaf from tatalaqqaf, assimilation of tāʾ into tāʾ is problematic: the resulting initial consonant would require hamzat al-waṣl, which does not enter imperfect verbs.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p235/r8.anchor: ومن خفف التاء من تلقف ومن شدد فقال: ما في يمينك تلقف، فإنما أراد: تتلقف وهذا يكون على تتلقف أنت أيها المخاطب، وعلى تتلقف في الآية أنه أدغم التاء في التاء، والإدغام في هذا ينبغي أن لا يجوز،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r1.claim: Hamzat al-waṣl does not prefix imperfect verbs or active participles; its few uses are forms with deleted endings that resemble imperatives, as in the cited examples.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r1.anchor: وإنما لم تدخل همزة الوصل على المضارع، كما لم تدخل على اسم الفاعل، لأن كل واحد منهما مثل الآخر،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r2.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r2.claim: Asked how an assimilator begins reciting, Ahmad ibn Musa said in effect that he starts with the light reading and leaves the assimilation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237/r2.anchor: وسألت أحمد بن موسى: كيف يبتدئ من أدغم؟ فقال كلاما معناه أنه يصير بالابتداء إلى قول من خفف ويدع الإدغام.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r1.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read kayd siḥr without the alif; the other readers use kayd sāḥir with an alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (كيد سحر) بغير ألف. وقرأ الباقون: كيد ساحر بألف .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r2.claim: The form ‘a magician’s plot’ is more direct because the plot belongs to the magician; ‘plot of magic’ works only by extension, meaning the plot of someone possessing magic.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r2.anchor: حجة: كيد ساحر أن الكيد للساحر في الحقيقة، وليس للسحر إلا أن تريد: كيد ذي سحر،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r3.speaker: الأعمش
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r3.claim: The reading kayd sāḥir is also reported for al-Aʿmash and is supported by the surrounding phrase repeating the same wording.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#2/r3.anchor: والسحر لا يمتنع أن يضاف إليه الكيد على التوسع، وزعموا أنه قراءة الأعمش.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244#2/r1.claim: The alif form sāḥir is an agent noun, “a magician's plot”; without alif, siḥr is the verbal noun, “magic.”
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244#2/r1.anchor: أنه جعله اسما لفاعل مشتقا من فعله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r1.speaker: النبال عن ابن كثير وقنبل
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r1.claim: Al-Nabbāl and Qunbul report Ibn Kathir with light tāʾ in تلقف; al-Bazzī and Ibn Fulayḥ transmit gemination of tāʾ and qāf.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r1.anchor: وروى النبال عن ابن كثير ﴿ ما في يمينك تلقف ﴾ خفيفة التاء كذلك قرأت على قنبل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r2.speaker: البزي وابن فليح عن ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r2.claim: Al-Bazzī and Ibn Fulayḥ report Ibn Kathir geminating both tāʾ and qāf in تلقف.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r2.anchor: وكان ابن كثير يشدد التاء والقاف فى رواية البزى وابن فليح

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r3.claim: These readers retain alif in ساحر; Hamza and al-Kisāʾī read the form without alif, كيد سحر.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر / كيد سحر / وقرأ حمزة والكسائى

NASHR:v2p231/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p231/r5.speaker: البزي
NASHR:v2p231/r5.claim: The section lists 31 future verbs whose initial tāʾ may double, across the cited passages; al-Bazzi transmits doubling in the stated routes, including the forms at 20:69 and 49:13.
NASHR:v2p231/r5.anchor: وذلك في إحدى وثلاثين تاء، وهي ولا تيمموا الخبيث هنا،

NASHR:v1p291/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p291/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p291/r1.claim: Among four sīn sites in this idgham inventory is كيد ساحر; al-Dani omitted it by oversight.
NASHR:v1p291/r1.anchor: كيد ساحر، عدد سنين، يكاد سنا ولم يذكر الداني

NASHR:v1p298/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p298/r1.speaker: أبو طاهر بن سوار وأبو العز القلانسي وابن الفحام
NASHR:v1p298/r1.claim: Several performance authorities describe indicating the movement during assimilation, arguing that the relevant articulation is shared with mīm and bāʾ; examples include يعلم ما, أعلم بما, and تعرف في وجوههم.
NASHR:v1p298/r1.anchor: غير واحد كأبي طاهر بن سوار في " المستنير "، وأبي العز

NASHR:v1p298/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p298/r2.speaker: أبو الكرم
NASHR:v1p298/r2.claim: Al-Karam uniquely says no gesture is needed when the neighboring vowel is ḍamma or a long wāw, but otherwise the movement is indicated by rawm or ishmam, as in يشفع عنده and كيد ساحر.
NASHR:v1p298/r2.anchor: وانفرد أبو الكرم في " المصباح " في الإشارة بمذهب آخر، فذكر

NASHR:v1p298/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p298/r3.speaker: أبو أحمد عبد السلام بن الحسين
NASHR:v1p298/r3.claim: Abu Ahmad reportedly required indicating the mīm in mīm-to-mīm assimilation and criticized omitting it; Ibn al-Jazari infers that the gesture means rawm.
NASHR:v1p298/r3.anchor: كان يأخذ بالإشارة في الميم عند الميم، وينكر على من يخل بذلك

NASHR:v1p298/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p298/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p298/r4.claim: When an assimilated consonant follows a weak quiescent letter, full assimilation is feasible; three options remain as in pause—intermediate madd, shortening, or a longer reading—with madd preferred for madd letters. The examples include الرحيم ملك and قوم موسى.
NASHR:v1p298/r4.anchor: فإن كان معتلا، فإن الإدغام معه ممكن حسن لامتداد الصوت به

NASHR:v1p298/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p298/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p298/r5.claim: With a sound quiescent consonant before the merger, full assimilation is difficult and later authorities often call it ikhfa or rawm; Ibn al-Jazari says both that and full idgham are sound, with full idgham established by early authorities, and rejects requiring izhar when rawm is absent.
NASHR:v1p298/r5.anchor: فإن الإدغام الصحيح معه يعسر؛ لكونه جميعا بين ساكنين

NASHR:v2p320/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p320/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p320/r1.claim: Readers agree on the al-Naba occurrence's form, following the subsequent verse-end pattern.
NASHR:v2p320/r1.anchor: على الحرف الذي في النبأ أنه كذلك اتباعا لرءوس الآي بعده

NASHR:v2p320/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p320/r9.speaker: ابن ذكوان وحفص والبزي
NASHR:v2p320/r9.claim: Ibn Dhakwan raises the fāʾ of تلقف; Hafs has sukūn on lām and a light qāf, while the others use jussive and doubled qāf. Al-Bazzi doubles the tāʾ in connected recitation.
NASHR:v2p320/r9.anchor: تلقف، فروى ابن ذكوان رفع الفاء، وروى حفص إسكان اللام

NASHR:v2p320/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p320/r10.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
NASHR:v2p320/r10.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read سحر without alif, with kasra on sīn and sukūn on ḥāʾ; the others read ساحر with alif, fatḥa on sīn, and kasra on ḥāʾ.
NASHR:v2p320/r10.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف، (سحر) بكسر السين

QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#1/r1.claim: Form V adds an intensive reflexive sense: the object eagerly snatches up or greedily devours the magicians' work of its own accord.
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#1/r1.anchor: instead of Form I — adds reflexive-intensive meaning

QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#2/r1.speaker: CE
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#2/r1.claim: An indicative ending in rafʿ makes it an independent statement that it swallows, rather than a jussive consequence of the imperative.
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#2/r1.anchor: Form V with indicative -u ending (rafʿ) rather than jussive — reads as independent statement ""it swallows up""

QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#3/r1.speaker: Assim
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#3/r1.claim: Assimilation of the first tāʾ into the second produces the heavy cluster, which the source says enacts the physical struggle of swallowing.
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:6#3/r1.anchor: Assimilated tāʾ: original tatalaqqaf with first tāʾ assimilated into second — Form VI or assimilated Form V

QIRAAT-ER:20:69:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:12#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:12#1/r1.claim: The verbal noun siḥr shifts the sense from a sorcerer's trick to sorcery as the act or craft itself, making the craft the scheming agent.
QIRAAT-ER:20:69:12#1/r1.anchor: verbal noun) instead of sāḥirin (active participle)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p19/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p19/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p19/r1.claim: Qatāda says that when Moses cast his staff, it became a serpent and swallowed their ropes and the things they had made.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p19/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ تلقف ما صنعوا ﴾ قال ألقاها موسى فتحولت حية تأكل حبالهم وما صنعوا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r1.claim: What is in Moses’ right hand is his staff; the wording recalls God’s earlier question about what he held.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r1.anchor: عصاك كما وقع فى سورة الأعراف وكان التعبير عنها بذلك لتذكيره ما وقع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r2.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r2.claim: Some scholars say ambiguity magnifies the staff as beyond familiar staffs and their ordinary effects, with strange consequences beyond human understanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r2.anchor: إنما اوثر الإبهام تهويلا لأمرها وتفخيما لشأنها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r3.claim: The same effect can be present when another passage narrates the order by meaning; this wording suits removing Moses’ fear and encouraging him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r3.anchor: ووقع حكاية الأمر فى مواضع أخر بالمعنى والواقع نفسه ما تضمن هذه النكتة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says right hand evokes good fortune and blessing; Alusi objects that the address to Moses was not in Arabic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : عبر بذلك دون عصاك لما فى اليمين من معنى اليمن والبركة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r5.claim: Another view takes the ambiguity as belittling the many ropes and staffs: a little stick will consume them; Alusi says this ignores the staff’s earlier extraordinary state.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r5.anchor: بأن المراد لا تبالى بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r6.claim: ما may be relative or descriptive; one analysis pairs the first possibility with the first construction and the second with the second.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r6.anchor: وما يحتمل أن ان تكون موصوفة ويحتمل أن تكون موصولة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r7.claim: The majority reading is jussive as an answer to the command; from لقف, it means to take deftly by hand or mouth, here by mouth, with feminine agreement because ما refers to the staff.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r7.anchor: بالفم وامراد هنا الثانى والتأنيث بكون ما عبارة عن العصا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r8.claim: The staff swallows ropes and staffs whose motion only seemed real; calling them what the magicians made belittles them and signals deception.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r8.anchor: أي تبتلع ما صنعوه من الحبال والعصى التى خيل إليك سعيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r9.claim: Most readers pronounce تلقف with an open lām and doubled qāf, dropping one of the two tāʾs from تتلقف.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r9.anchor: بفتح اللام وتشديد القاف وإسقاط إحدى التاءين من ( تتلقف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r10.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAmir has the same form but raises the verb as a new explanatory clause or a circumstantial clause for the agent or object of ألق.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر كذلك إلا أنه رفع الفعل على أن الجملة مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r11.claim: The command completes the prohibition by explaining how Moses will prevail: the staff consumes the falsehood that triggered his hidden fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r11.anchor: وجملة الأمر معطوفة على النهى متممة بما فى حيزها لتعليل موجبه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r12.claim: Some argue this proves Moses did not fear people doubting the staff’s miracle, since the reply would otherwise promise their belief; Alusi says the argument merits consideration.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#4/r12.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن هذا صريح فى أن خوفه عليه السلام لم يكن من مخالجة الشك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r1.claim: This clause explains why the staff swallows their work; ما may mean what they made, a thing they made, or their making.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r1.anchor: وما إما موصولة أو موصوفة أو مصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r2.claim: On the nominative reading, كيد ساحر is the predicate of إن; ساحر is indefinite so the genitive is likewise indefinite as the context requires.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r2.anchor: بالرفع على أنه خبر إن أى كيد جنس الساحر وتنكيره للتوسل به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r3.claim: Though الساحر could be definite yet generic, there is no need to identify the magic’s kind: the preceding context does so and the point is its unreality.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r3.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لا حاجة إلى تعيين جنسه فانه مما علم من قوله تعالى ( يخيل ) الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r4.claim: A proposal that indefiniteness belittles the trick is unsuitable, implies ranks of magic, and conflicts with their magic being called great; apparent greatness can coexist with inner triviality.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r4.anchor: لا يناسب المقام ولأنه يفيد انقسام السحر إلى حقير وعظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r5.claim: Another explanation makes الساحر indefinite to avoid the idea of a particular, known sorcerer.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r6.speaker: مجاهد، حميد، زيد بن على
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r6.claim: Mujahid, Humayd, and Zayd ibn ʿAli read كيد in the accusative as the object of صنعوا, with ما functioning as an expletive.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وزيد بن على عليهم الرحمة ( كيد ) بالنصب على أنه مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r7.speaker: حمزة، الكسائى، أبو بحرية، الأعمش، طلحة، ابن أبى ليلى، خلف، ابن عيسى الأصبهانى، ابن جبير الأنطاكى، ابن جرير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r7.claim: These readers have سِحْر with kasra on sīn and a still ḥāʾ: possessor of magic, a sorcerer called magic by intensification, or a genitive showing the trick is of magic’s kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائى وأبو بحرية والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبى ليلى وخلف فى اختياره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r8.claim: For the explanatory genitive, the commentator of al-Hadi describes the relation as lām and al-Sharif’s apparent position as min; some require a particular overlap between terms.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p229/r8.anchor: من إضافة العام الى الخاص وهى على معنى اللام عند شارح الهادى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r1.claim: No sorcerer succeeds wherever he may be; حيث is a place adverb used universally, completing the explanation for Moses’ command.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r1.anchor: حيث كان وأين أقبل فحيث ظرف مكان أريد به التعميم من تمام التعليل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r2.claim: The text does not say the staff is a divine miracle, although that could strengthen the reasoning, because its status is already evident.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r2.anchor: ولم يتعرض لشأن العصا وكونها معجزة الهية مع ما فى ذلك من تقوية التعليل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r3.claim: A report collected by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh from Jundub says the Prophet ordered that a sorcerer be killed when caught, then recited this verse; Alusi gives no grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) إذا أخذتم الساحر فاقتلوه ثم قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r4.speaker: فرقة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230/r4.claim: One group reads أين أتى instead of حيث أتى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r2.claim: What is in Moses' right hand is his staff.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r3.claim: Talaqqaf means to swallow or gulp down.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r4.claim: Ibn Amir reads the fāʾ with ḍamma; the other readers use the jussive as the response to the command.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر "تلقف" برفع الفاء هاهنا، وقرأ الآخرون بالجزم على جواب الأمر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read siḥr, without alif and with kasra on the sīn, while the others read sāḥir; attributing the trick to its agent is preferable, though the verbal-noun construction is also Arabic.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r5.anchor: هكذا قرأ حمزة والكسائي: بكسر السين بلا ألف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r6.claim: The magician does not prosper anywhere on earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r6.anchor: {ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى} من الأرض،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says a magician never succeeds wherever he may be.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا يسعد حيث كان.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r8.claim: Another gloss takes the phrase to mean wherever the magician attempts his trick.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r3.claim: Leaving the staff unnamed may belittle it beside the magicians' implements, or magnify it: the small object in Moses' hand has greater effect than their large tools.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r3.anchor: أبهمه ولم يقل عصاك تحقيرا لها أي لا تبال بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r4.claim: The staff swallows their tricks through God's power; تلقف derives from تتلقف with one ت omitted, and its prefix can mark feminine agreement or address when the cause is assigned the action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r4.anchor: تبتلعه بقدرة الله تعالى، وأصله تتلقف

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r5.speaker: ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان وحفص
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir through Ibn Dhakwān reads the verb in the nominative as a circumstantial clause or new sentence; Ḥafṣ reads it jussive and light, from لقفت meaning تلقفت.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان بالرفع على الحال

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r6.claim: What they made means what they contrived and fabricated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r6.anchor: { إنما صنعوا } أن الذي زوروا وافتعلوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r7.claim: Another reading puts كيد in the accusative, taking ما as a particle that makes صنعوا transitive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r7.anchor: وقرىء بالنصب على أن ما كافة وهو مفعول صنعوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r8.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read سحر: it can mean possessor of magic, call a magician magic for emphasis, or explain the genitive as the magic itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «سحر» بمعنى ذي سحر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r9.claim: The singular ساحر is generic, as is الساحر in the following clause; al-ʿAjjāj's phrase سعي دنيا illustrates the indefinite construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r9.anchor: وإنما وحد الساحر لأن المراد به الجنس المطلق

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r10.speaker: العجاج
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r10.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj's line يوم ترى النفوس ما أعدت في سعي دنيا طالما قد مدت is cited as evidence for the indefinite construction around سعي دنيا.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r10.anchor: كقول العجاج: يوم ترى النفوس ما أعدت في سعي دنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r11.claim: حيث أتى means wherever he is or wherever he approaches.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r11.anchor: { حيث أتى } حيث كان وأين أقبل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r3.claim: The staff in Moses’ right hand recalls the staff first mentioned when God asked what it was during their initial meeting.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r3.anchor: من هذه العصا التي قلنا لك أول ما شرفناك بالمناجاة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r4.claim: The form suggests forceful, energetic swallowing at a speed scarcely perceived; the omitted tāʾ signals that swiftness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r4.anchor: بقوة واجتهاد مع سرعة لا تكاد تدرك - بما أشار غليه حذف التاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r5.claim: The magicians’ display was the product of extensive training and long practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r5.anchor: فعلوه بعد تدرب كبير عليه وممارسة طويلة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r6.claim: The indefinite singular a magician’s trick belittles the whole company and denies its work substance, whether made by one magician or many; a plural would stress their number instead.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r6.anchor: اي كيد سحري لا حقيقة له ولا ثبات

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r7.claim: Magic cannot prevail wherever it goes because it produces only what has no reality.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r7.anchor: فإنه إنما يفعل ما لا حقيقة له

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r8.claim: The staff swallowed the display without growing thicker, despite the great quantity of ropes and staffs, so witnesses recognized Moses’ truth and the magicians’ falsehood.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r8.anchor: من غير أن يظهر عليها زيادة في ثخن ولا غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r1.claim: Most readers pronounce talqaf with fatḥa on lām and a doubled qāf; Ḥafṣ reads it with a still lām and an ungeminated qāf, from laqifa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تلقف بفتح اللام وتشديد القاف .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r2.claim: In innamā, mā is relative; kaydu sāḥir is the predicate, so the sentence simply reports what they did rather than restricting it. The written connection does not reflect the distinction earlier scribes observed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r2.anchor: و { كيد ساحر } خبر ( إن ) . والكلام إخبار بسيط لا قصر فيه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r3.claim: Most read sāḥir with an alif after sīn; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read siḥr with kasra on sīn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { كيد ساحر بألف بعد السين . وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف كيد سحر بكسر السين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r4.claim: The clause continues the previous sentence and is circumstantial of its pronoun: magic fails because sustained reflection and composure expose it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r4.anchor: فهي معطوفة عليها وحال من ضمير { إنما صنعوا } ، أي لا ينجح الساحر حيث كان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r5.claim: The definite noun denotes the generic, familiar class: no sorcerer succeeds by sorcery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r5.anchor: وتعريف { الساحر تعريف الجنس لقصد الجنس المعروف ، أي لا يفلح بها كل ساحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r6.claim: Atā was chosen instead of kāna or ḥalla because most magicians had been brought from across Egypt, and because it preserves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r6.anchor: واختير فعل أتى } دون نحو : حيث كان ، أو حيث حل ، لمراعاة كون معظم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r7.claim: The phrase generalizes over every place the sorcerer attends with his magic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r7.anchor: وتعميم { حيث أتى } لعموم الأمكنة التي يحضرها ، أي بسحره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r8.claim: The denial concerns success in sorcery, not a sorcerer’s trade or other affairs; the generic negative also universalizes the relevant acts and places.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r8.anchor: وتعليق الحكم بوصف الساحر يقتضي أن نفي الفلاح عن الساحر في أمور السحر لا في تجارة أو غيرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r5.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r5.claim: The majority read talqaf jussively as the response to the command, with a doubled qāf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r5.anchor: قرأ جمهور القراء «تلقف» بالجزم على جواب الأمر وبشد القاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads talqaf as a circumstantial clause, referring flexibly either to what was cast or to the staff itself; Ibn Atiyya compares 5:95.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحده «تلقف» وهو في موضع الحال ويصح أن يكون من الملقى على اتساع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r7.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r7.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads with a still lām and light qāf, making the verb feminine to agree with the staff intended by what is in the right hand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r7.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم «تلقف» بسكون اللام وتخفيف القاف وأنث الفعل وهو مسند إلى ما في اليمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r8.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r8.claim: Al-Bazzī reports Ibn Kathīr doubling the tāʾ as though the form were tatalaqqaf, assimilating one tāʾ into the other.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r8.anchor: وروى البزي عن ابن كثير أنه كان يشدد التاء من «تلقف» كأنه أراد تتلقف فأدغم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r9.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects the doubled-tāʾ reading reported from Ibn Kathīr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r9.anchor: وأنكر أبو علي هذه القراءة ع ويشبه أن قارئها إنما يلتزمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests the reader may use this form only in connected recitation, where introducing an alif is unnecessary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r10.anchor: ويشبه أن قارئها إنما يلتزمها في الوصل حيث يستغنى عن جلب ألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r11.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r11.claim: The majority read kayd in the nominative in the phrase kayd sāḥir.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r12.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the second word as siḥr, making the phrase kayd siḥr.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r13.claim: A group reads kayd in the accusative and siḥr, taking mā as an impeditive particle and kayd as the object of ṣanaʿū.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r13.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «كيد» بالنصب «سحر» وهذا على أن «ما» كافة و «كيد» منصوب ب صنعوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r14.claim: The nominative kayd is explained by taking mā as the relative pronoun meaning ‘that which.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r15.claim: Yufliḥ means to remain and to attain one’s aim.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r16.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r16.claim: A group takes the phrase to mean that a sorcerer is killed wherever found, this being the punishment for failure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r16.anchor: وقالت فرقة معناه أن الساحر يقتل حيث ثقف ع وهذا جزاء من عدم الفلاح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r17.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r17.claim: A group reads ayn atā instead of ḥaythu atā; Ibn Atiyya says their meanings are close.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r17.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «أين أتى» والمعنى بهما متقارب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r18.speaker: رُوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r18.claim: An unnamed account says Pharaoh watched from an elevated pavilion eighty cubits high, with the people gathered below.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r18.anchor: وروي من قصص هذه الآية أن فرعون، لعنه الله، جلس في عليه له طولها ثمانون ذراعا والناس تحته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r19.speaker: رُوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r19.claim: The account says seventy thousand magicians cast enough ropes and staffs to equal the load of three hundred camels, creating a terrifying spectacle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r19.anchor: وجاء سبعون ألف ساحر فألقوا من حبالهم وعصيهم ما فيه وقر ثلاثمائة بعير فهال الأمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r20.speaker: رُوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r20.claim: Moses’ staff became a growing serpent, crossed the river or sea with its tail, swallowed the props, frightened Pharaoh, then returned to a staff; the magicians recognized truth and believed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r20.anchor: ثم إن موسى عليه السلام ألقى عصاه من يده فاستحالت ثعبانا وجعلت تنمو حتى روي أنها عبرت النهر بذنبها، وقيل البحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r1.claim: What Moses has in his right hand is his staff.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وألق ما في يمينك يعني العصا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads talaqqaf with a raised fāʾ and doubled qāf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر تلقف ما برفع الفاء وتشديد القاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r3.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r3.claim: Hafs from ʿAsim reads talaqqaf with a light qāf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r3.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم تلقف خفيفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir doubles the tāʾ in talaqqaf, understood as tata-laqqaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r4.anchor: وكان ابن كثير يشدد التاء من تلقف يريد تتلقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وسعيد بن جبير وأبو رجاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Abu Rajaʾ read talqamu with mīm; the author discussed it at 7:117.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وسعيد بن جبير وأبو رجاء تلقم بالميم وقد شرحناها في الأعراف 117

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r6.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf read kaydu al-siḥr, “the plot of magic.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف / كيد السحر /

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r7.claim: The remaining readers have kaydu sāḥir, “a magician's plot.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو عمران الجوني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Abu ʿImran al-Jawni read kayda with the dāl in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو عمران الجوني إنما صنعوا كيد بنصب الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains that a magician does not prosper wherever he may be.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس لا يسعد حيثما كان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r10.claim: Another explanation takes yufliḥ as “does not succeed” or “does not win.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r11.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r11.claim: Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Bajali reports the Prophet's instruction to kill a sorcerer if caught; the Prophet then quotes this verse to say the sorcerer is unsafe wherever found.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#2/r11.anchor: وروى جندب بن عبدالله البجلي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إذا أخذتم الساحر فاقتلوه ثم قرأ ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى قال لا يأمن حيث وجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r2.claim: God immediately inspired Moses to throw what was in his right hand, namely his staff.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r2.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليه في الساعة الراهنة أن {وألق ما في يمينك} يعني: عصاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r3.speaker: author
