IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r3.claim: The staff became a huge, terrifying serpent with eyes, limbs, neck, head, and fangs; it pursued and swallowed every rope and stick before the crowd in broad daylight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r3.anchor: وذلك أنها صارت تنينا (4) عظيما هائلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r4.claim: The public miracle made the proof clear and nullified the sorcerers' work: what they devised was a magician's scheme, and a magician never succeeds wherever he comes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r4.anchor: فقامت المعجزة، واتضح البرهان، وبطل ما كانوا يعملون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r5.claim: The Prophet reportedly ordered that a sorcerer be killed when caught and recited this verse; al-Tirmidhi transmitted the report's basis both as a Companion statement and as Prophetic, with no grading given here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r5.anchor: عن الحسن، عن جندب بن عبد الله البجلي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "إذا أخذتم -يعني الساحر-فاقتلوه"

JISHUMI:v7p4692/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r2.claim: Ibn Amir reads talaqqaf with a doubled qāf and nominative fāʾ; Hafs from Asim has a light form with silent lām and jussive fāʾ; others double qāf with jussive fāʾ. The source derives it from tata-laqqafu and explains the jussive as the result of casting the staff.
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر: تلقف بالتشديد ورفع الفاء، وقرأ حفص عن عاصم: تلقف بسكون اللام وجزم الفاء

JISHUMI:v7p4692/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read kayd siḥr without alif and with kasra on sīn; other readers have kayd sāḥir with alif and fatḥa.
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: كيد سحر بغير ألف وكسر السين، وقرأ الباقون بالألف وفتح السين

JISHUMI:v7p4692/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda says attributing the plot to a sorcerer is more apt than attributing it to magic, though the latter is grammatically possible; all readers agree الساحر has an alif in the next phrase.
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: إضافة الكيد إلى الرجل أولى من إضافته إلى السحر وإن كان ذلك لا يمتنع في العربية

JISHUMI:v7p4692/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r5.claim: Ilqāʾ is throwing or casting something away; it is synonymous with ṭarḥ, nabdh, and ramy.
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r5.anchor: الإلقاء: مصدر ألقى يلقي إلقاء إذا نبذه وطرحه، والإلقاء والطرح والنبذ والرمي نظائر

JISHUMI:v7p4692/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r10.claim: Laqifa, talaqqafa, and iltaqafa mean to seize quickly or swallow.
JISHUMI:v7p4692/r10.anchor: يقال: لقفت الشيء ألقفه، وتلقفته والتقفته إذا أخذته بسرعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r1.claim: The indefinite wording generalizes the trick: what they made was sorcery, in worldly or otherworldly activity of that kind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r1.anchor: المراد تنكير الأمر ، كأنه قيل : إن ما صنعوا كيد سحري . وفي سعي دنيوي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r2.claim: The phrase means wherever the sorcerer comes or acts, like “wherever he was sent,” “whichever way he went,” and “wherever.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r2.anchor: { حيث أتى } كقولهم : حيث سير ، وأية سلك ، وأينما كان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r3.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r3.claim: A saying attributed to ʿUmar illustrates the general indefinite use: “not in a worldly matter nor in another matter.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r3.anchor: وفي حديث عمر رضي الله عنه : لا في أمر دنيا ولا في أمر آخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r4.claim: An unattributed poetic line, “in worldly striving that has long been extended,” supplies an example of worldly usage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77/r4.anchor: في سعي دنيا طالما قد مدت

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r11.claim: The staff was to take their work into its mouth and swallow it quickly.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r12.claim: It is said the staff swallowed a load of ropes and staffs carried by three hundred camels; Moses then took it and it returned to its former shape.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r12.anchor: فقيل إنها ابتلعت حمل ثلاثمائة بعير من الحبال والعصي , ثم أخذها موسى ورجعت عصا كما كانت

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r13.speaker: وهب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r13.claim: Wahb says Moses' staff was made from an ʿawsaj thorn tree.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r13.anchor: أنها كانت من عوسج , قاله وهب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the staff came from Paradise and that Moses killed ʿUj ibn ʿAnaq with it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r14.anchor: من الجنة , قاله ابن عباس , قال : وبها قتل موسى عوج بن عناق

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r1.claim: The object in Moses’ right hand is his staff; when he threw it, it became a serpent.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r1.anchor: يعنى عصاه، ففعل، فإذا هى حية

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r2.claim: “Taltaqaf” means “swallow”; the serpent swallowed the ropes and staffs produced by the magicians.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r2.anchor: يقول: تلقم { ما صنعوا } من السحر حتى تلقمت الحبال والعصى

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r3.claim: The magicians’ production was a magician’s trick, while what Moses did was not magic.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r3.anchor: إن الذى عملوا هو عمل ساحر، يعنى كبيرهم، وما صنع موسى فليس بسحر

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r4.claim: A magician cannot succeed wherever he may be.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ and Ibn Dhakwān read with still lām, fatḥa on fāʾ, and light qāf; others read doubled qāf.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r1.anchor: بسكون اللام وافاء وتخفيف القاف حفص ابن ذكوان الباقون تلقف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r2.claim: Their trick is swallowed when Moses casts his staff; the wording omits “your staff” either to honor its power or belittle their many ropes and staffs against one stick.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r2.anchor: زورا وافتعلوا أي اطرح عصاك تبتلع عصيهم وحبالهم ولم يقل عصاك تعظيما لها أي لا تحتفل بما صنعوا فإن ما في يمينك أعظم منها أو تحقيرا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r3.claim: Kufans other than ʿĀṣim read siḥr, meaning magician or those possessing magic, or equating deeply immersed magicians with magic.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r3.anchor: ﴿ إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ﴾ كوفي غير عاصم سحر بمعنى ذي سحر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r4.claim: Kayd is nominative under both readings; mā can be relative or a verbal noun.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r4.anchor: وكيد بالرفع على القراءتين وما موصولة أو مصدرية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r5.claim: The singular sāḥir denotes the class rather than a number: no magician succeeds wherever he goes.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r5.anchor: وإنما وجد ساحر ولم يجمع لان القصد في هذا الكلام إلى معنى الجنسية لا إلى معنى العدد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r6.claim: After Moses' staff swallowed their work, the magicians recognized the sign and prostrated in the next verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#6/r6.anchor: فالقى موسى عصاه فتلقفت ما صنعوا فلعظم ما رأوا من الآية وقعوا إلى السجود فذلك قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r5.claim: Not naming the staff may diminish it rhetorically: Moses should disregard the many ropes and staffs and cast the small, solitary stick, which by God's power will swallow them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r5.anchor: فجائز أن تكون تصغيرا لها أي لا تبال بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r6.claim: Alternatively, the omission magnifies the staff: the many large objects are negligible beside what Moses holds, which will erase them by God's permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r6.anchor: وجائز أن يكون تعظيما لها أي لا تحفل بهذه الأجرام الكثيرة الكبيرة فإن في يمينك شيئا أعظم منها كلها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r7.claim: Talaqqaf in the jussive answers the imperative, with an understood condition: if you cast it, it will swallow them; the verb means to take and swallow.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r7.anchor: و«تلقف» بالجزم جواب الأمر كأنه قال: إن تلقه تتلقف أي تأخذ وتبتلع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r8.speaker: السلمي وحفص
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r8.claim: Al-Sulami and Hafs read talaqqaf with a quiescent lam, from laqifa yalqafu.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r8.anchor: وقرأ السلمي وحفص «تلقف» ساكنة اللام من لقف يلقف لقفا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r9.speaker: ابن ذكوان وأبو حيوة الشامي ويحيى بن الحرث
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r9.claim: Ibn Dhakwan, Abu Haywa al-Shami, and Yahya ibn al-Harith read with the ta deleted and the fa nominative, meaning the staff itself swallows.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن ذكوان وأبو حيوة الشامي ويحيى بن الحرث «تلقف» بحذف التاء ورفع الفاء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r10.claim: The imperative may address Moses or, alternatively, the staff.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r11.claim: Laqf is taking something quickly; the expression also describes a quick, deft person.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r11.anchor: يقال: لقفت الشيء بالكسر ألقفه لقفا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r12.speaker: يعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r12.claim: Yaqub gives laqif thaqif as an expression for a quick, capable, deft man.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r12.anchor: عن يعقوب: يقال رجل لقف ثقف أي خفيف حاذق.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r13.claim: Laqf can also mean a wall falling; a basin may cave in at its base and widen. Talaqqafa, talaqqama, and talahhama are synonymous for swallowing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r13.anchor: واللقف بالتحريك سقوط الحائط. ولقد لقف الحوض لقفا أي تهور من أسفله واتسع.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r14.claim: Ma ṣanaʿū and innamā ṣanaʿū refer to what they made.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r14.anchor: أي الذي صنعوه وكذا { إنما صنعوا } أي إن الذي صنعوه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r15.speaker: الكوفيون إلا عاصما
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r15.claim: The Kufans except Asim read kaydu in the nominative and siḥr with kasra on sin and sukun on ha.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r15.anchor: كيد } بالرفع «سحر» بكسر السين وإسكان الحاء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r16.claim: On the nominative reading, kayd may be annexed to siḥr without ellipsis, or an omitted phrase may mean a plot belonging to a possessor of magic.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r16.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون الكيد مضافا إلى السحر على الإتباع من غير تقدير حذف

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r17.claim: The other readers put kayd in the accusative as the object of ṣanaʿū; mā is restrictive, no pronoun is elided before sāḥir, and kayd is truly annexed to the magician.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r17.anchor: بوقوع الصنع عليه، و«ما» كافة ولا تضمر هاء «ساحر»

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r18.claim: The hamza of anna may be opened with causal force: because what they made is a magician's plot.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r18.anchor: ويجوز فتح «أن» على معنى لأن ما صنعوا كيد ساحر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r19.claim: The magician does not succeed or escape wherever he comes from on earth; alternatively, wherever he schemes.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r19.anchor: أي لا يفوز ولا ينجو حيث أتى من الأرض. وقيل: حيث احتال.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r20.claim: The commentary refers readers to al-Baqara for the ruling on magicians and the meaning of magic.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r20.anchor: وقد مضى في «البقرة» حكم الساحر ومعنى السحر فتأمله هناك.

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r1.claim: What is in your right hand means the staff; the deliberately unspecified wording magnifies it and signals that its extraordinary effects distinguish it from ordinary staffs.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r1.anchor: {وألق ما في يمينك} أي : عصاك والإبهام لتفخيم شأنها

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r2.claim: Talqaf is jussive as the response to the imperative.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r2.anchor: {تلقف ما صنعوا} بالجزم جواب للأمر من لقفه

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r3.claim: The verb means to gulp or swallow quickly; al-Mufradāt says it can mean taking something by pulling, whether with the mouth or hand.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r3.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : لقفت الشيء القفه وتلقفته تناولته بالجذب

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r4.claim: The verb is feminine because mā here stands for the staff.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r4.anchor: والتأنيث لكون ما عبارة عن العصا

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r5.claim: Ṣunʿ is doing something skillfully: every craft is an act, but not every act is craft, and craft is not attributed to animals or inanimate things as general action is.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r5.anchor: والصنع إجادة الفعل فكل صنع فعل وليس كل فعل صنعا

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r6.claim: The staff will swallow ropes and sticks whose apparent motion and lightness frightened Moses; calling them what the magicians made belittles their work as deceit.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r6.anchor: والتعبير عنها بما صنعوا للتحقير والإيذان بالتمويه والتزوير

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r7.claim: Mā can be a relative pronoun or an indefinite description, yielding either what they made or something they made.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r7.anchor: ما موصولة أو موصوفة أي : إن الذي صنعوه أو إن شيئا صنعوه

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r8.claim: Kayd sāḥir is nominative as the predicate of inna; its indefinite form in an annexation belittles the sorcerer's kind of scheme.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r8.anchor: بالرفع على أنه خبر لأن أي : كيد جنس الساحر ومكره وحيلته

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r9.claim: A scheme can be praiseworthy or blameworthy, although the word is more commonly used for blameworthy plotting; the same usage tendency applies to istidrāj and makr.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r9.anchor: والكيد ضرب من الاحتيال يكون محمودا أو مذموما وإن كان يستعمل في المذموم أكثر

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r10.claim: Magicians as a class never attain their aim wherever they practice magic; this completes the reason the staff defeats their work.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r10.anchor: {ولا يفلح الساحر} أي : لا يدرك بغيته هذا الجنس

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r11.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r11.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the staff as God's own making and scheme, while the magicians' work is theirs; their craft cannot prosper against His firm design.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r11.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن ما في يمينك هو مصنوعي

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r12.claim: Worldly success means survival, wealth, power, and honor; afterlife success means permanence without death, wealth without poverty, honor without humiliation, and knowledge without ignorance. Worldly success alone ends in loss.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r12.anchor: واعلم أن الفلاح دنيوي وهو الظفر بالسعادات التي تطيب بها حياة الدنيا

BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r13.claim: Bursevī illustrates the claim with a student who objects to his teacher and later prospers materially but remains a loser; he applies the lesson to wrongdoers and opponents.
BURSEVI:v5p309#2/r13.anchor: ألا ترى أن من قال لأستاذه لم أي : اعترض عليه لن يفلح أبدا

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r14.claim: Calling it “what is in your right hand” rather than naming the staff may belittle it: Moses need not fear the many ropes and sticks but can throw his small rod.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r14.anchor: جاز أن يكون تصغيرا لها أي لا تبال بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم وألق العويد الفرد الصغير الجرم الذي بيمينك

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r15.claim: Alternatively, the wording may exalt the object in Moses’ hand as greater than all the opponents’ many objects.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r15.anchor: وجائز أن يكون تعظيما لها أي لا تحتفل بهذه الأجرام الكثيرة فإن في يمينك شيئا أعظم منها كلها

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r16.speaker: العامة
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r16.claim: The common reading has jazm and a doubled qāf, linking the command to throwing with the result that the staff catches their fabrications.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r16.anchor: قراءة العامة تلقف بالجزم والتشديد أي فألقها تتلقفها

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r17.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r17.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads with a doubled qāf and ḍamma on the fāʾ, as a circumstantial description (“throw it catching”) or an independent clause.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r17.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر تلقف بالتشديد وضم الفاء على معنى الحال أي ألقها متلقفة أو بالرفع على الاستئناف

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r18.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r18.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads with a quiescent lām and no doubling, meaning to take something into the mouth and swallow it quickly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r18.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم بسكون اللام مع التخفيف أي تأخذ بفيها ابتلاعا بسرعة

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r19.claim: Laqf and talaqquf both convey taking something in and swallowing it quickly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r19.anchor: واللقف والتلقف جميعا يرجعان إلى هذا المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r20.claim: Here ṣanaʿū means they fabricated or falsified; Arabic calls a lie manufactured or contrived speech.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r20.anchor: وصنعوا ههنا بمعنى اختلقوا وزوروا والعرب تقول في الكذب : هو كلام مصنوع وموضوع

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r21.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r21.claim: The following verse says the magicians fell prostrate, confirming that Moses’ staff became a serpent and swallowed their work; the swallowing implies great size and strength.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r21.anchor: وفي قوله : { فألقى السحرة سجدا } ( طه : 70 ) دلالة على أنه ألقى العصا

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r22.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r22.claim: The magicians recognized that Moses’ sign exceeded human craft because of its movement, impossible growth, visible organs, swallowing all their objects, and return to a small wooden staff.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r22.anchor: وقد حكى عن السحرة أنهم عند التلقف أيقنوا بأن ما جاء به موسى

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r23.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r23.claim: Moses’ sign is a divine miracle, while the magicians’ work is only false trickery, so the two cannot truly compete.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r23.anchor: ثم بين سبحانه وتعالى أن ما صنعوا كيد ساحر والمعنى أن الذي معك يا موسى معجزة إلهية والذي معهم تمويهات باطلة

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r24.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r24.claim: “A sorcerer’s plot” is read with nominative or accusative kayd; the nominative parses mā as relative, while the accusative treats it as particle of limitation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r24.anchor: بالرفع والنصب فمن رفع فعلى أن ما موصولة ومن نصب فعلى أنها كافة

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r25.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r25.claim: Another reading, kayd siḥr, can mean an owner of sorcery, owners of sorcery, or sorcerers so immersed that they are sorcery itself.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r25.anchor: وقرىء كيد سحر بمعنى ذي سحر أو ذوي سحر

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r26.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r26.claim: The wording specifies sorcery because a plot may be sorcery or something else, just as one specifies a quantity or a discipline.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r26.anchor: كما يبين المائة بدرهم ونحوه علم فقه وعلم نحو

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r6.claim: The doubled, raised reading derives from tatalaqqafu by dropping one tāʾ; the raised form supplies an understood fa or describes what is in Moses' hand.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r6.anchor: فالحجة لمن شدد ورفع أنه أراد تتلقف فأسقط إحدى التاءين تخفيفا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r7.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r7.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r7.claim: The doubled jussive and the light jussive are both answers to the imperative; the light form derives from laqifa yalqafu.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r7.anchor: والحجة لمن خفف وجزم أنه أخذه من لقف يلقف وجزمه بالجواب أيضا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r8.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r8.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r8.claim: Ibn Kathīr is reported to double this tāʾ and similar forms in more than thirty places.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r8.anchor: فقد روى عن ابن كثير بتشديد هذه التاء وما شاكلها في نيف وثلاثين موضعا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r9.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r9.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r9.claim: The doubled raised form can suppress an understood fa, meaning cast what is in your right hand and it will gulp, or make the verb circumstantial to mā.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r9.anchor: والحجة لمن شدد ورفع أنه أضمر الفاء فكأنه قال الق ما في يمينك فإنها بلقف أو يجعله حالا من ما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r10.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads تلقف with nominative fāʾ and doubled qāf.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r10.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر وحده ﴿ تلقف ﴾ برفع الفاء وتشديد القاف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r11.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r11.speaker: حفص عن عاصم، الباقون وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r11.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim has sukūn on lām, light qāf, and jussive; the others and Abū Bakr read it jussive.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r11.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم ﴿ تلقف ﴾ بتسكين اللام وتخفيف القاف والجزم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r10.claim: Calling the staff ما recalls God’s earlier question about what Moses held, reassuring him that the object would again assume its miraculous state; God therefore does not simply say to throw the staff.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r10.anchor: وعبر عن العصا ب { ما } الموصولة تذكيرا له بيوم التكليم إذ قال له : { وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r10.claim: The public miracle gave all observers clear premises: events need a cause, and humans cannot create huge animals instantaneously and then shrink them, proving a world-governing Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r10.anchor: حدثت أمور فلا بد لها من مؤثر والعلم بذلك ضروري

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r11.claim: Razi says the deniers knew these premises but chose ignorance; reason alone is insufficient, since God must create premises, awareness of their order, and conclusions in hearts, so all proceeds by divine decree.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r11.anchor: العقل والدليل لا يكفي بل لا بد من مدبر يخلق هذه المقدمات في القلوب

THALABI:v6p252/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r13.claim: Talaqqaf means to swallow, gulp down, and engulf what the magicians made.

THALABI:v6p252/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r15.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v6p252/r15.claim: The Kufans read the word with kasra and no alif, while the rest read sāḥir with an alif; Abū ʿUbayd prefers the latter because attributing the plot to a magician is preferable, though both forms are Arabic.
THALABI:v6p252/r15.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة بكسر السين من غير ألف، وقرأ الباقون: ساحر بالألف على فاعل

TABATABAI:20:76-79/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:76-79/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:20:76-79/r9.claim: Jundub al-Bajali reports the Prophet saying to kill a sorcerer when caught, then citing the verse as meaning the sorcerer is safe nowhere; al-Tabataba'i says this application is unclear in context.
TABATABAI:20:76-79/r9.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه عن جندب بن عبد الله البجلي

THALABI:v6p252/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r14.claim: What the magicians made is a magician's plot.
THALABI:v6p252/r14.anchor: إنما صنعوا يعني إن الذي صنعوا كيد ساحر

THALABI:v6p252/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r16.claim: The phrase means wherever the magician is on earth, or wherever he contrives.
THALABI:v6p252/r16.anchor: ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى من الأرض، وقيل: معناه حيث احتال

MAJAZ:v2p22/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p22/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p22/r6.claim: Ḥaythu atā means wherever he is or goes.
MAJAZ:v2p22/r6.anchor: ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى» (69) أي حيث كان..
